giris.satir: Good health to you, gatekeeper. I am Physician Evhaduddin of the Konya Darushifa; I set fractures, treat fevers, and decipher ancient manuscripts. As plague and turmoil spread along the caravan roads, I took my medicine chest and my young daughter toward this secluded village. If you would establish an infirmary and study room, hear my terms.

secenekler.metin: Both healing and learning are honored here, Master Evhaduddin; what do you ask from the village chest?
Who is the young woman beside you? What do you stipulate for shelter and apprenticeship?

pazarlik_ucret.satir: To set out my mortar bowls, lancets, and theriac jars, I ask twenty coins from the village public treasury—I take nothing from your personal pouch. In return, I unlock second-tier infirmary and study room knowledge for this village.

secenekler.metin: We understand the treasury fee; what of your daughter and housing?
We pay the twenty coins from the village chest, Master Physician; enter and set up the infirmary.
Our chest cannot spare twenty coins, Master Physician; go in peace.

pazarlik_ev_aile.satir: Beside me is my young daughter Meryem; we are two souls and ask a dry roof. If your beds are full we can wait briefly in the open, provided my medicine chest stays dry. Meryem knows herbs and bandages; apprentice her to me in the infirmary and in five nights she will be a half-physician.

secenekler.metin: Accepted, Master Evhaduddin; enter with your daughter Meryem, and let her train in the infirmary.
We cannot meet your terms, Master Physician; seek another town.

kabul_sonuc.satir: Healing comes from God, effort from us, gatekeeper. Know from the outset: I am a surgeon and scholar; I do not take up a spear for night sentry duty on the wall. My watch is beside the wounded and the manuscripts.

ret_sonuc.satir: The choice is yours, gatekeeper. When winter fever or arrow wounds knock at your gate, you will wish for Evhaduddin of Konya.
